verses.zh: 摩西去告诉以色列众人
verses.en: Then Moses went[NOTE:1] and spoke these words[NOTE:2] to all Israel.
notes: For the MT reading וַיֵּלֶךְ (vayyelekh, “he went”), the LXX and Qumran have וַיְכַל (vayekhal, “he finished”): “So Moses finished speaking,” etc. The difficult reading of the MT favors its authenticity.
In the MT this refers to the words that follow (cf. NIV, NCV).

verses.zh: 说：「我现在一百二十岁了，不能照常出入；耶和华也曾对我说：『你必不得过这约旦河。』
verses.en: He said to them, “Today I am 120 years old. I am no longer able to get about,[NOTE:1] and the Lord has said to me, ‘You will not cross the Jordan.’
notes: Or “am no longer able to lead you” (NIV, NLT); Heb “am no longer able to go out and come in.”

verses.zh: 耶和华―你们的　神必引导你们过去，将这些国民在你们面前灭绝，你们就得他们的地。约书亚必引导你们过去，正如耶和华所说的。
verses.en: As for the Lord your God, he is about to cross over before you; he will destroy these nations before you, and you will dispossess them. As for Joshua, he is about to cross before you just as the Lord has said.

verses.zh: 耶和华必待他们，如同从前待他所灭绝的亚摩利二王西宏与噩以及他们的国一样。
verses.en: The Lord will do to them just what he did to Sihon and Og, the Amorite kings, and to their land, which he destroyed.

verses.zh: 耶和华必将他们交给你们；你们要照我所吩咐的一切命令待他们。
verses.en: The Lord will deliver them over to you, and you will do to them according to the whole commandment I have given you.

verses.zh: 你们当刚强壮胆，不要害怕，也不要畏惧他们，因为耶和华―你的　神和你同去。他必不撇下你，也不丢弃你。」
verses.en: Be strong and courageous! Do not fear or tremble before them, for the Lord your God is the one who is going with you. He will not fail you or abandon you!”

verses.zh: 摩西召了约书亚来，在以色列众人眼前对他说：「你当刚强壮胆！因为，你要和这百姓一同进入耶和华向他们列祖起誓应许所赐之地；你也要使他们承受那地为业。
verses.en: Then Moses called out to Joshua[NOTE:1] in the presence of all Israel, “Be strong and courageous, for you will accompany these people to the land that the Lord promised to give their ancestors,[NOTE:2] and you will enable them to inherit it.
notes: The Hebrew text includes “and said to him.” This has not been included in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “fathers” (also in v. 20).

verses.zh: 耶和华必在你前面行；他必与你同在，必不撇下你，也不丢弃你。不要惧怕，也不要惊惶。」
verses.en: The Lord is indeed going before you—he will be with you; he will not fail you or abandon you. Do not be afraid or discouraged!”

verses.zh: 摩西将这律法写出来，交给抬耶和华约柜的祭司利未子孙和以色列的众长老。
verses.en: Then Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the Levitical priests, who carry the ark of the Lord’s covenant, and to all Israel’s elders.

verses.zh: 摩西吩咐他们说：「每逢七年的末一年，就在豁免年的定期住棚节的时候，
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] commanded them: “At the end of seven years, at the appointed time of the cancellation of debts,[NOTE:2] at the Feast of Shelters,[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Moses.” The pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons.

The Hebrew term שְׁמִטָּה (shemittah), a derivative of the verb שָׁמַט (shamat, “to release; to relinquish”), refers to the procedure whereby debts of all fellow Israelites were to be canceled. Since the Feast of Tabernacles celebrated God’s own deliverance of and provision for his people, this was an appropriate time for Israelites to release one another. See note on this word at Deut 15:1.

For the regulations on this annual festival see Deut 16:13-15.tn The Hebrew phrase חַג הַסֻּכּוֹת (khag hassukkot, “festival of huts” [or “shelters”]) is traditionally known as the Feast of Tabernacles. See note on the name of the festival in Deut 16:13.

verses.zh: 以色列众人来到耶和华―你　神所选择的地方朝见他。那时，你要在以色列众人面前将这律法念给他们听。
verses.en: when all Israel comes to appear before the Lord your God in the place he chooses, you must read this law before them[NOTE:1] within their hearing.
notes: Heb “before all Israel.”

verses.zh: 要招聚他们男、女、孩子，并城里寄居的，使他们听，使他们学习，好敬畏耶和华―你们的　神，谨守、遵行这律法的一切话，
verses.en: Gather the people—men, women, and children, as well as the resident foreigners[NOTE:1] in your villages—so they may hear and thus learn about and fear the Lord your God and carefully obey all the words of this law.
notes: The ger (גֵּר) “foreign resident” or “naturalized citizen,” (see Exod 12:19 and Deut 29:10-13) could make sacrifices (Lev 17:8; 22:18; Num 15:14) and participate in Israel’s religious festivals: Passover Exod 12:48; Day of Atonement Lev 16:29; Feast of Weeks Deut 16:10-14; Feast of Tabernacles/Temporary Shelters Deut 31:12.

verses.zh: 也使他们未曾晓得这律法的儿女得以听见，学习敬畏耶和华―你们的　神，在你们过约旦河要得为业之地，存活的日子，常常这样行。」
verses.en: Then their children, who have not known this law,[NOTE:1] will also hear about and learn to fear the Lord your God for as long as you live in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess.”
notes: The phrase “this law” is not in the Hebrew text, but English style requires an object for the verb here. Other translations also supply the object which is otherwise implicit (cf. NIV “who do not know this law”; TEV “who have never heard the Law of the Lord your God”).

verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「你的死期临近了；要召约书亚来，你们二人站在会幕里，我好嘱咐他。」于是摩西和约书亚去站在会幕里。
verses.en: Then the Lord said to Moses, “The day of your death is near. Summon Joshua and present yourselves in the tent[NOTE:1] of meeting[NOTE:2] so that I can commission him.”[NOTE:3] So Moses and Joshua presented themselves in the tent of meeting.
notes: The LXX reads “by the door of the tent” in line with v. 10 but also, perhaps, as a reflection of its tendency to avoid over-familiarity with Yahweh and his transcendence.

Heb “tent of assembly” (אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד, ʾohel moʿed); this is not always the same as the tabernacle, which is usually called מִשְׁכָּן (mishkan, “dwelling-place”), a reference to its being invested with God’s presence. The “tent of meeting” was erected earlier than the tabernacle and was the place where Yahweh occasionally appeared, especially to Moses (cf. Exod 18:7-16; 33:7-11; Num 11:16, 24, 26; 12:4).
Heb “I will command him.”

verses.zh: 耶和华在会幕里云柱中显现，云柱停在会幕门以上。
verses.en: The Lord appeared in the tent in a pillar of cloud that[NOTE:1] stood above the door of the tent.
notes: Heb “and the pillar of cloud.” This phrase was not repeated in the translation; a relative clause was used instead.

verses.zh: 耶和华又对摩西说：「你必和你列祖同睡。这百姓要起来，在他们所要去的地上，在那地的人中，随从外邦神行邪淫，离弃我，违背我与他们所立的约。
verses.en: Then the Lord said to Moses, “You are about to die,[NOTE:1] and then these people will begin to prostitute themselves with the foreign gods of the land into which they[NOTE:2] are going. They[NOTE:3] will reject[NOTE:4] me and break my covenant that I have made with them.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “lie down with your fathers” (so NASB); NRSV “ancestors.”

Heb “he.” Smr, LXX, and the Targums read the plural “they,” which is necessary in any case in the translation because of contemporary English style. The third person singular also occurs in the Hebrew text twice more in this verse, three times in v. 17, once in v. 18, five times in v. 20, and four times in v. 21. Each time it is translated as third person plural for stylistic reasons.
Heb “he.” Smr, LXX, and the Targums read the plural “they.” See note on the first occurrence of “they” in v. 16.
Or “abandon” (TEV, NLT).
Heb “him.” Smr, LXX, and the Targums read the plural “them.” See note on the first occurrence of “they” in v. 16.

verses.zh: 那时，我的怒气必向他们发作；我也必离弃他们，掩面不顾他们，以致他们被吞灭，并有许多的祸患灾难临到他们。那日他们必说：『这些祸患临到我们，岂不是因我们的　神不在我们中间吗？』
verses.en: At that time[NOTE:1] my anger will erupt against them,[NOTE:2] and I will abandon them and hide my face from them until they are devoured. Many disasters and distresses will overcome[NOTE:3] them[NOTE:4] so that they[NOTE:5] will say at that time, ‘Have not these disasters[NOTE:6] overcome us[NOTE:7] because our[NOTE:8] God is not among us[NOTE:9]?’
notes: Heb “on that day.” This same expression also appears later in the verse and in v. 18.
Heb “him.” Smr, LXX, and the Targums read the plural “them.” See note on the first occurrence of “they” in v. 16.
Heb “find,” “encounter.”
Heb “him.” Smr, LXX, and the Targums read the plural “them.” See note on the first occurrence of “they” in v. 16.
Heb “he.” Smr, LXX, and the Targums read the plural “they.” See note on the first occurrence of “they” in v. 16.
Heb “evils.”
Heb “me.” Smr, LXX, and the Targums read the plural “us,” which is necessary in any case in the translation because of contemporary English style.
Heb “my.”
Heb “me.” Smr, LXX, and the Targums read the plural “us,” which is necessary in any case in the translation because of contemporary English style.

verses.zh: 那时，因他们偏向别神所行的一切恶，我必定掩面不顾他们。
verses.en: But I will certainly[NOTE:1] hide myself at that time because of all the wickedness they[NOTE:2] will have done by turning to other gods.
notes: The Hebrew text uses the infinitive absolute for emphasis, which the translation indicates with “certainly.”
Heb “he.” Smr, LXX, and the Targums read the plural “they.” See note on the first occurrence of “they” in v. 16.

verses.zh: 现在你要写一篇歌，教导以色列人，传给他们，使这歌见证他们的不是；
verses.en: Now write down for yourselves the following song and teach it to the Israelites. Put it into their very mouths so that this song may serve as my witness against the Israelites!

verses.zh: 因为我将他们领进我向他们列祖起誓应许那流奶与蜜之地，他们在那里吃得饱足，身体肥胖，就必偏向别神，事奉他们，藐视我，背弃我的约。
verses.en: For after I have brought them[NOTE:1] to the land I promised to their[NOTE:2] ancestors—one flowing with milk and honey—and they[NOTE:3] eat their fill[NOTE:4] and become fat, then they[NOTE:5] will turn to other gods and worship them; they will reject me and break my covenant.
notes: Heb “him.” Smr, LXX, and the Targums read the plural “them.” See note on the first occurrence of “they” in v. 16.
Heb “his.” Smr, LXX, and the Targums read the plural “their.” See note on the first occurrence of “they” in v. 16.
Heb “he.” Smr, LXX, and the Targums read the plural “they.” See note on the first occurrence of “they” in v. 16.
Heb “and are satisfied.”
Heb “he.” Smr, LXX, and the Targums read the plural “they.” See note on the first occurrence of “they” in v. 16.

verses.zh: 那时，有许多祸患灾难临到他们，这歌必在他们面前作见证，他们后裔的口中必念诵不忘。我未领他们到我所起誓应许之地以先，他们所怀的意念我都知道了。」
verses.en: Then when[NOTE:1] many disasters and distresses overcome them[NOTE:2] this song will testify against them,[NOTE:3] for their[NOTE:4] descendants will not forget it.[NOTE:5] I know the[NOTE:6] intentions they have in mind[NOTE:7] today, even before I bring them[NOTE:8] to the land I have promised.”
notes: Heb “Then it will come to pass that.”
Heb “him.” Smr, LXX, and the Targums read the plural “them.” See note on the first occurrence of “they” in v. 16.
Heb “him.” Smr, LXX, and the Targums read the plural “them.” See note on the first occurrence of “they” in v. 16.
Heb “his.” Smr, LXX, and the Targums read the plural “their.” See note on the first occurrence of “they” in v. 16.
Heb “it will not be forgotten from the mouth of his seed.”
Heb “his.” Smr, LXX, and the Targums read the plural “their.” See note on the first occurrence of “they” in v. 16.
Heb “which he is doing.”
Heb “him.” Smr, LXX, and the Targums read the plural “them.” See note on the first occurrence of “they” in v. 16.

verses.zh: 当日摩西就写了一篇歌，教导以色列人。
verses.en: So on that day Moses wrote down this song and taught it to the Israelites,

verses.zh: 耶和华嘱咐嫩的儿子约书亚说：「你当刚强壮胆，因为你必领以色列人进我所起誓应许他们的地；我必与你同在。」
verses.en: and the Lord[NOTE:1] commissioned Joshua son of Nun, “Be strong and courageous, for you will take the Israelites to the land I have promised them, and I will be with you.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “he.” Since the pronoun could be taken to refer to Moses, the referent has been specified as “the Lord” in the translation for clarity. See also the note on the word “you” later in this verse.

The LXX reads, “as the Lord promised them, and he will be with you.” This relieves the problem of Moses apparently promising to be with Joshua as the MT reads on the surface (“I will be with you”). However, the reading of the LXX is clearly an attempt to clarify an existing obscurity and therefore is unlikely to reflect the original.

verses.zh: 摩西将这律法的话写在书上，及至写完了，
verses.en: When Moses finished writing on a scroll the words of this law in their entirety,

verses.zh: 就吩咐抬耶和华约柜的利未人说：
verses.en: he[NOTE:1] commanded the Levites who carried the ark of the Lord’s covenant,
notes: Heb “Moses.” The pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons to avoid redundancy.

verses.zh: 「将这律法书放在耶和华―你们　神的约柜旁，可以在那里见证以色列人的不是；
verses.en: “Take this scroll of the law and place it beside the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God. It will remain there as a witness against you,

verses.zh: 因为我知道你们是悖逆的，是硬着颈项的。我今日还活着与你们同在，你们尚且悖逆耶和华，何况我死后呢？
verses.en: for I know about your rebellion and stubbornness.[NOTE:1] Indeed, even while I have been living among you to this very day, you have rebelled against the Lord; you will be even more rebellious after my death![NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “stiffness of neck” (cf. KJV, NAB, NIV). See note on the word “stubborn” in Deut 9:6.
Heb “How much more after my death?” The Hebrew text has a sarcastic rhetorical question here; the translation seeks to bring out the force of the question.

verses.zh: 你们要将你们支派的众长老和官长都招聚了来，我好将这些话说与他们听，并呼天唤地见证他们的不是。
verses.en: Gather to me all your tribal elders and officials so I can speak to them directly about these things and call the heavens and the earth to witness against them.

verses.zh: 我知道我死后，你们必全然败坏，偏离我所吩咐你们的道，行耶和华眼中看为恶的事，以手所做的惹他发怒；日后必有祸患临到你们。」
verses.en: For I know that after I die you will totally[NOTE:1] corrupt yourselves and turn away from the path I have commanded you to walk. Disaster will confront you in future days because you will act wickedly[NOTE:2] before the Lord, inciting him to anger because of your actions.”[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew text uses the infinitive absolute for emphasis, which the translation indicates with “totally.”
Heb “do the evil.”
Heb “the work of your hands.”

verses.zh: 摩西将这一篇歌的话都说与以色列全会众听。
verses.en: Then Moses recited the words of this song from start to finish in the hearing of the whole assembly of Israel:

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing
is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: DEUTERONOMY 31:1-6

1So Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel. 2And he said to them, "I am a
hundred and twenty years old today; I am no longer able to come and go, and the Lord has said to me, 'You shall not cross this Jordan.'
3It is the Lord your God who will cross ahead of you; He will destroy these nations before you, and you shall dispossess them.
Joshua is the one who will cross ahead of you, just as the Lord has spoken. 4The Lord will do
to them just as He did to Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their land, when He destroyed them. 5The Lord will
deliver them up before you, and you shall do to them according to all the commandments which I have commanded you. 6Be strong and courageous, do not
be afraid or tremble at them, for the Lord your God is the one who goes with you. He will not fail you or forsake you."

31:1 "spoke these words" Possibly this should be "finished speaking," following the Septuagint and some
manuscripts of the Dead Sea Scrolls (cf. NRSV, REB). This is the end of Moses' three sermons. The UBS Text Project, p. 299,
gives the MT a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEPTUAGINT

31:2 "I am a hundred and twenty" Moses' life of 120 years (cf. Deut. 34:7) can be divided into three 40 year segments. Moses was

- 40 years being prepared at the royal academies of Egypt

- 40 years in the desert training for his call

- 40 years from the time of the burning bush to the present (cf. Exod. 7:7 and Acts 7:23ff)

Why mention his age? These are possible reasons:

- in Egyptian literature 110 years was the age of wise men, but in Syria it was 120 years

- age limit of Gen. 6:3

- another excuse of Moses for why he will not lead them into the Promised Land (see note below)

▣ "I am no longer able to come and go" This is a Hebrew idiom for

- vitality (Josh. 14:11; NRSV, TEV, NJB, JPSOA)

- military activity (Jewish Study Bible, p. 438)

However, old age had not taken away Moses' strength, cf. Deut. 34. Possibly this was an excuse (cf. Deut. 1:37)
related to Moses' public disobedience recorded in Num. 20:11-12. Deuteronomy 3:23-29 records Moses' pleading with
God to let him enter the Promised Land (cf. Deut. 32:48-52).

31:3 "the Lord your God who will cross ahead of you" YHWH fights for them, though
they must prepare for battle and participate (cf. Deut. 31:3-6, i.e. holy war terminology). Moses was a tool used by God. God,
Himself, was the one who delivered the people. In reality it is YHWH, not Joshua, who goes into battle ahead of His people!

▣ "Joshua is the one who will cross ahead of you" A new leader was needed because of Moses'
disobedience. God will be with Joshua, but he too must perform his covenant obligations (cf. Deut. 1:38; 3:28).

31:6 "Be strong and courageous" This verse has several imperatival forms:

- "be strong" ‒ BDB 304, KB 302, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Deut. 31:7,23

- "be courageous" ‒ BDB 54, KB 65, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Deut. 31:7,23

- "do not be afraid" ‒ BDB 431, KB 432, negated Qal IMPERFECT, used in a JUSSIVE sense

- "do not tremble" ‒ BDB 791, KB 888, negated Qal IMPERFECT, used in a JUSSIVE
sense, cf. Deut. 1:29; 7:21; 20:3; Josh. 1:9

Numbers 1 and 2 are repeated by Moses to Joshua in Deut. 31:7 and numbers 3 and 4 are repeated in
Deut. 31:8 (#4 is parallel, but a different VERB, "be dismayed," BDB 369, KB 365, Qal
IMPERFECT).

A proper attitude and faith are essential! There are giants in the land, but YHWH is with His people (cf. Deut. 31:3,4,5,6).

▣ "He will not fail you or forsake you"

- YHWH goes with them (i.e. "walks," BDB 229, KB 246, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE)

- YHWH will not fail them (i.e. "abandon," BDB 951, KB 1276, Hiphil IMPERFECT)

- YHWH will not forsake them ("leave," BDB 736 I, KB 806, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Gen. 28:15)

This promise is repeated to Joshua in Josh. 1:5 and is repeated as a promise to NT believers in
Heb. 13:5! Our hope is in the unchanging gracious character of YHWH (e.g. Exod. 34:6; Neh. 9:17; Ps. 103:8; 145:8; Joel 2:13; Mal. 3:6)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: DEUTERONOMY 31:7-8

7Then Moses called to Joshua and said to him in the sight of all Israel, "Be strong and courageous,
for you shall go with this people into the land which the Lord has sworn to their fathers to give them, and you shall give it to them as
an inheritance. 8The Lord is the one who goes ahead of you; He will be with you. He will not fail you or forsake you. Do
not fear or be dismayed."

31:7 This is a public transfer of power! This is the fulfillment of Deut. 1:38 and 3:28!

▣

NASB, JPSOA
"for you shall go with this people"

NKJV
"for you must go with this people"

NRSV
"for you are the one who will go with this

people"

TEV
"You are the one who will lead these

people"

LXX
"For you will go before this people"

Peshitta

The MT is reflected in the NASB. The UBS Text Project, pp. 299-300, gives this a "D" rating (i.e. highly
doubtful). It suggests the translation of the Peshitta (Vulgate).

31:8 "He will be with you" This is restated, "I will be with you," in Deut. 31:23! The promise of YHWH's personal
presence is the greatest blessing that can be given (cf. Exod. 3:12; 4:12,15; 33:14-16; Deut. 4:37; Josh. 1:5). It is the reason
why His leaders and people should not be fearful of anyone or anything!

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: DEUTERONOMY 31:9-13

9So Moses wrote this law and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi who carried the ark of the
covenant of the Lord, and to all the elders of Israel. 10Then Moses commanded them, saying, "At the end of
every seven years, at the time of the year of remission of debts, at the Feast of Booths, 11when all Israel comes to appear before the
Lord your God at the place which He will choose, you shall read this law in front of all Israel in their hearing. 12Assemble
the people, the men and the women and children and the alien who is in your town, so that they may hear and learn and fear the Lord
your God, and be careful to observe all the words of this law. 13Their children, who have not known, will hear and learn to fear the Lord
your God, as long as you live on the land which you are about to cross the Jordan to possess."

31:9 "Moses wrote this law" Several times in the Pentateuch it says, "Moses wrote" (cf. Exod. 17:14; 24:4,22;
34:1,27,28; Num. 17:2,3; 33:2; Deut. 4:13; 5:22; 31:9,22). Moses gave the Law to Israel to standardize the will of YHWH
for future generations.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOSES' AUTHORSHIP OF THE PENTATEUCH

▣ "to the priests, the sons of Levi" It is interesting that there is some divergency in exactly who are "priests":

- tribe of Levi (always)

- sons of Aaron (often)

All priests are Levites, but not all Levites are priests. In Deuteronomy the distinction between priests and
Levites is removed (i.e. Deut. 18:1).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LEVITICAL PRIESTS

▣ "to the elders" This refers to tribal elders. In this verse Moses entrusts the law to Israel's religious and
secular (i.e. tribal) leaders (cf. Deut. 27:1). However, in reality, all of Israel's leaders and laws were seen as religious
(i.e. YHWH's will). There was no secular versus sacred in Israel. All was sacred because all belonged to YHWH! There were
special days and special places, but all of life was regulated by divine decrees!

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELDERS

31:10 There are two dates referred to in this verse:

- one was every year, the Feast of Booths

- Exod. 23:16-17; 34:22

- Lev. 23:33-43

- Deut. 16:13-15

- one was every seventh year (i.e. the Sabbatical year)

- Exod. 23:10,11

- Lev. 25:1-7

- Deut. 15:1-6

Here, Moses adds to the regular rituals the annual reading of the covenant.

The Feast of the Booths (i.e. #1) was an annual event meant to remind Israel of YHWH's gracious
and powerful acts of deliverance from Egypt and His provision and presence during the wilderness wanderings.

This festival of thanksgiving for deliverance/freedom, as well as the freedom from debt ceremony, occurred every
seventh year (i.e. #2, Sabbath year, cf. Leviticus 25).

The combination of these two freedom events was a perfect time to review the Mosaic law covenant with this gracious,
covenant-making God (i.e. YHWH)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FEASTS OF ISRAEL

31:11 "the place which He will choose" This verse in Moses' day referred to the gathering of all males three times
a year (cf. Leviticus 23) at the tabernacle (cf. Exod. 20:24; Deut. 12:5,11,13; 14:25; 15:20; 16:7,16; 17:8,10; 18:6; 26:2).

Later it would refer to the central shrine located in Jerusalem.

▣ "you shall read this law in front of all Israel" This was a covenant renewal event. The Law was clearly
revealed (i.e. read) and Israel committed herself to its keeping! Everyone in Israel's society was present (cf. Deut. 31:12-13), even
the newest generation (i.e. of Bar Mitzvah at age 13, e.g. Isa. 7:16; see SPECIAL TOPIC: AGE OF ACCOUNTABILITY).

The law was not only for a later king nor current leaders, but for all the people through their generation
and even resident aliens!

31:12 "may hear. . .learn. . .fear" Notice the progression of VERBS:

- "hear" ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERFECT, common in Deuteronomy, meaning "to hear so as to do";
see SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

- "learn" ‒ BDB 540, KB 531, Qal IMPERFECT

- "fear" ‒ BDB 431, KB 432, Qal IMPERFECT with waw (see last paragraph below; see SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR)

- "be careful to observe" (see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)

- BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal PERFECT with waw

- BDB 793, KB 889, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT

Notice that #1,2,3 are repeated in Deut. 31:13 to relate to the new generation, which did not as yet know (BDB 393, KB 390,
Qal PERFECT). This law was meant to be known and kept through multiple generations of Israelis.

In some ways this progression reminds me of Ezra (cf. Ezra 7:10). Israel is to fear or revere (BDB 431) YHWH
(cf. Deut. 4:10; 14:23; 17:19), but not fear anyone or anything else!

- the tent of meeting described in Exod. 33:7-11, erected outside of the camp of Israel, where Moses went to meet with YHWH

- it showed YHWH's presence

- it led the Israelites from place to place

- it shaded them by day

- it lit up their camp by night

Once they crossed Jordan, YHWH's presence was manifested over the Ark of the Covenant, but the cloud disappeared.

The term is a combination of "neck" (BDB 791) and "stiff" or "hard" (BDB 904). Israel is often described

In a sense Deut. 31:27-29 are a prophecy, based on the past actions of Israel. This same kind of prophecy
is also found in Josh. 24:19-20. Israel's best efforts were not enough. The first covenant would fail to restore the intended
intimacy between YHWH and His highest creation (i.e. mankind) in the Garden of Eden. It would take the New Covenant (cf. Jer. 31:31-34;
Ezek. 36:22-36) based on YHWH's actions. Mankind was incurably rebellious (cf. Gen. 6:5; 8:21; Jer. 17:9; Rom. 1-3; Gal. 3).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are
meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why is God changing leaders?

- How is God's foreknowledge and man's choice related in this chapter?

- Why did Israel turn away from God?
